# AccessNexus (npm: accessnexus)

> Schema-first engine for Supabase. You describe tables, access rules (RLS), roles,
> triggers and RPCs once in TypeScript (`accessnexus.schema.ts`); AccessNexus generates the
> SQL migrations, Row-Level Security policies, triggers, Postgres functions and a typed
> client SDK — with Supabase RLS best practices built in. This file is the complete
> reference for AI coding agents. Package version: 0.1.0. Requires Node.js >= 20.

## Mental model (read first)

- `accessnexus.schema.ts` is the single source of truth for the database. To add a table,
  column, policy, role rule, trigger or RPC: edit the schema, never SQL.
- Everything under the output folders (default `generated/`) and the SDK files
  (`client.ts`, `types.ts`) is derived. Never hand-edit it — regenerate.
- Every table gets Row-Level Security (ENABLE + FORCE). A table WITHOUT `policies` is
  deny-all for the API (anon and signed-in users get nothing; only the service role and
  SECURITY DEFINER code reach it) — `validate` warns `NO_POLICIES`. Every table the app reads
  or writes from the client needs policies. `enableRLS: false` turns RLS off (anyone with
  the anon key can read and write the table; `validate` warns `RLS_DISABLED`) — never use it
  unless the user asked for an open table.
- `push` is the only command that touches the real database. Preview with
  `push --dry-run` and only push when the user asked for it. `push` refuses generated SQL
  that is out of date with the schema, and refuses pending migrations that drop
  tables/columns or change column types unless `--allow-destructive` is passed (ask the
  user first — that deletes data). It never runs the seed unless `--seed` is passed.
- All commands are non-interactive when stdin is not a TTY, accept `--json`, and use
  exit codes 0 = ok, 1 = fixable error (read `error.hint`), 2 = AccessNexus bug.

## Standard agent workflow

1. Edit `accessnexus.schema.ts`.
2. `npx accessnexus validate --json` — fix every issue with `"severity": "error"` (each has
   `path` and `hint`); treat warnings as bugs unless deliberate (`RLS_DISABLED`,
   `PUBLIC_WRITE`, `USER_ROW_INSERT_OPEN`, `TENANT_PARENT_UNCHECKED`, ...). In manual mode
   TypeScript does not check column names inside `policy.*` / `definePermissions`
   (`policy.isOwner('usr_id')` compiles): `validate` does (`UNKNOWN_COLUMN`), so never skip it.
3. `npx accessnexus diff --json` — review the SQL that will change. Run it BEFORE generate:
   diff compares the schema with the files on disk, so right after `generate` it is empty.
   (`diff --check` exits 1 when generated files are stale; use it in CI.)
4. `npx accessnexus generate --json` — writes SQL + SDK; reports created/updated/unchanged.
   To review afterwards, use `git diff generated/`.
5. Before ANY push: `npx accessnexus diff --against-db --json` (or `push --dry-run --json`,
   which runs the same plan when a database URL is set). It rehearses the push against the
   live database in a rolled-back transaction and lists what would really change (tables,
   columns, policies, triggers, functions, grants) with `before`/`after`. Review
   `riskyChanges` with the user (volatility or `SET search_path` changes, widened policy
   roles, dropped policies, lost defaults, type changes, RLS disabled), plus `blockers` and
   `failed`. Then `npx accessnexus push --json` when asked.
   If `generate`/`diff`/`push` report `destructive` statements, tell the user what data
   would be lost; a rename should be a rename in the schema, not remove + add.

New project: `npx accessnexus init --yes` (add `--no-introspect` to skip the database,
or `--db-url <postgres-url>` to import existing tables, RLS policies and functions). In an
empty folder `init --yes` first creates a minimal `package.json` (`"type": "module"`).

## Project files

- `accessnexus.schema.ts` — `export default defineSchema({...})` (required). It may import
  sibling files (`import { cols } from './db/cols.js'`): schema, config and seed files are
  bundled with esbuild, which ships with accessnexus — no tsx/ts-node needed. The snippets here
  write relative imports with a `.js` extension (`'./accessnexus.schema.js'` resolves to
  `accessnexus.schema.ts`), which works with every `moduleResolution` (`bundler`, `node16`,
  `nodenext`); extensionless imports only typecheck under `bundler`.
- `accessnexus.config.ts` — optional `export default defineConfig({...})` (paths, prefix).
- `accessnexus.seed.ts` — optional `export default defineSeed(schema, {...})`.
- `generated/migrations/` — `<timestamp>__init.sql`, `<timestamp>__changes.sql`, `.snapshot.json`.
- `generated/policies/<table>_rls.sql`, `generated/triggers/<table>_triggers.sql`, `generated/rpcs/rpcs.sql`.
- `generated/sdk/` (or `output.sdk`) — `types.ts` + `client.ts` (derived, never edit).
- The client wrapper `init` writes next to them (`index.ts`, or `server.ts` + `browser.ts`
  on Next.js) is YOUR file: `generate` never touches it; edit env var names freely.
- Database URL for push/seed: `--url` (alias `--db-url`, the flag `init` uses), else `adapterOptions.dbUrlEnv`, else
  `ACCESSNEXUS_DB_URL`, `SUPABASE_DB_URL`, `DATABASE_URL` (`.env` and `.env.local` are loaded).
  For Supabase use the "Session pooler" connection string (Dashboard → Connect).
- `push`/`seed` need the `pg` driver (optional peer dependency): `npm install -D pg`.
- `push` must run as a role with BYPASSRLS — on Supabase the `postgres` user of the
  connection string. The generated SECURITY DEFINER helpers and the audit/soft-delete
  triggers rely on their owner bypassing RLS.

## defineSchema + table (manual mode)

Columns are type strings; append `?` for nullable. The object form adds `default`,
`unique`, `check`, `references`, `onDelete`. Table names and columns are lowercase snake_case
(one leading `_` is allowed: `_internal`, `_pix_crc16`) and cannot be reserved SQL keywords (`order`, `user`, `group`, `limit`, ... → `orders`, `user_id`).

`default` and `check` are RAW SQL, emitted verbatim: `default: 'now()'`, `default: '0'`,
`default: 'false'`. A string or enum literal needs its own single quotes inside the JS string:
`status: { type: "enum('todo','done')", default: "'todo'" }` — `default: 'todo'` would be
`DEFAULT todo` (a column name) and `validate` reports `INVALID_DEFAULT`.

```ts
// accessnexus.schema.ts
import { defineSchema, policy, table, trigger } from 'accessnexus';

export default defineSchema({
  profiles: table({
    // Public profile only: the email stays in auth.users. Every signed-in user can read
    // this table, so never put private data (email, phone, address) in it.
    columns: {
      id: 'uuid',
      name: 'text',
      bio: 'text?',
      created_at: { type: 'timestamptz', default: 'now()' },
      updated_at: 'timestamptz?',
    },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { id: 'auth.users.id' },
    triggers: [trigger.updatedAt('updated_at')],
    policies: {
      select: policy.isAuthenticated(),   // private columns? use policy.isOwner('id')
      insert: policy.isOwner('id'),
      update: policy.isOwner('id'),
      delete: policy.none(),
    },
  }),

  posts: table({
    columns: {
      id: 'uuid',
      author_id: 'uuid',
      title: 'text',
      status: "enum('draft','published')",
      tags: 'text[]?',
      deleted_at: 'timestamptz?',
    },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { author_id: 'profiles.id' },
    indexes: [{ columns: ['author_id', 'status'] }],
    softDelete: 'deleted_at',
    policies: {
      // Soft-deleted rows stay readable through RLS: exclude them from the public branch
      // (see the soft-delete note under trigger.* builders).
      select: policy.any([
        policy.isOwner('author_id'),
        policy.custom("status = 'published' AND deleted_at IS NULL"),
      ]),
      insert: policy.isOwner('author_id'),
      update: policy.isOwner('author_id'),
      delete: policy.isOwner('author_id'),
    },
  }),
});
```

Column types: `uuid text varchar int smallint bigint serial float decimal numeric boolean json
jsonb date timestamp timestamptz time text[] int[] uuid[]`, `numeric(p)` / `numeric(p,s)` (e.g.
`'numeric(10,2)'`, no space) and `"enum('a','b')"`; add `?` for NULL. `float` is
`DOUBLE PRECISION`; use `numeric(p,s)` for money.
A `uuid` primary key defaults to `gen_random_uuid()`; a `bigint` one becomes an identity.

Table options: `columns` (required), `primaryKey`, `compositePrimaryKey` (`['org_id', 'user_id']`
→ `PRIMARY KEY (org_id, user_id)`, instead of `primaryKey`; not with `softDelete`), `references` (`column: 'table.column'`
or `'schema.table.column'`, e.g. `'auth.users.id'`), `onDelete` (per referencing column:
`'cascade' | 'set null' | 'restrict' | 'no action'`), `policies` (`select`/`insert`/`update`/
`delete`), `triggers`, `indexes` (`{ columns, unique?, name? }`), `softDelete` (column; DELETE
becomes `SET <column> = NOW()` and the SDK hides deleted rows), `enableRLS` (only `false`
matters: it turns RLS off and opens the table — never set it unless asked).

Foreign keys default to `ON DELETE NO ACTION`: deleting a parent that still has children
fails with a foreign key error. Say what should happen to the children:

```ts
import { defineSchema, policy, table } from 'accessnexus';

export default defineSchema({
  projects: table({
    columns: { id: 'uuid', owner_id: 'uuid', name: 'text' },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { owner_id: 'auth.users.id' },
    policies: { select: policy.isOwner('owner_id'), insert: policy.isOwner('owner_id'), update: policy.isOwner('owner_id'), delete: policy.isOwner('owner_id') },
  }),
  tasks: table({
    columns: {
      id: 'uuid',
      project_id: { type: 'uuid', references: 'projects.id', onDelete: 'cascade' }, // tasks go with the project
      assignee_id: 'uuid?',
      owner_id: 'uuid',
    },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { assignee_id: 'auth.users.id', owner_id: 'auth.users.id' },
    onDelete: { assignee_id: 'set null' },                                         // table-level map works too
    policies: { select: policy.isOwner('owner_id'), insert: policy.isOwner('owner_id'), update: policy.isOwner('owner_id'), delete: policy.isOwner('owner_id') },
  }),
});
```

`'set null'` needs a nullable column. `'cascade'` into a `softDelete` table is rejected
(`CASCADE_INTO_SOFT_DELETE`): the soft delete would keep the children pointing at a deleted
parent — use `'restrict'` and soft-delete the children first. Cascades run as the table owner
(RLS does not stop them), so only cascade where deleting the parent should delete everything.

## Database mode (columns from Supabase types)

If the project already has Supabase-generated `database.types.ts`, list only the tables
to configure and omit `columns` (mode is detected when no table declares columns). AccessNexus
then generates RLS, triggers, RPCs and the SDK, but no DDL migrations.

```ts
import { defineSchema, policy, rpc } from 'accessnexus';
import type { Database } from './database.types.js';

export default defineSchema<Database>({
  profiles: {
    policies: {
      // Each user reads only their own profile. Use policy.isAuthenticated() only when
      // the table holds no private columns (email, phone...): every account could list them.
      select: policy.isOwner('id'),
      update: policy.isOwner('id'),
    },
  },
}, {
  rpcs: { get_stats: rpc() },
});
```

## policy.* builders

One rule per operation. `select`/`delete` compile to `USING` (which rows are visible /
deletable); `insert` to `WITH CHECK` (what may be written); `update` to `USING` (which rows
may be targeted) plus an explicit `WITH CHECK` with the same rule (what the row may become),
so an update can never move a row out of the rule. An operation without a rule is denied
once the table has policies. String values in rules are quoted safely.

Policy target role (`TO ...`): a `select` policy is granted `TO public` when some branch can be
true for an anonymous visitor (`policy.public()`, `policy.custom(...)`, a column-to-column
`matchesField`), else `TO authenticated`. Writes are `TO public` only when an explicit
`policy.public()` decides them. The predicate always decides; you never set the role.

```ts
import { policy } from 'accessnexus';

// (SELECT auth.uid()) IS NOT NULL
export const signedIn = policy.isAuthenticated();
// TRUE — everyone, including anonymous visitors (use for reads only)
export const everyone = policy.public();
// FALSE — nobody through the API (service role and triggers bypass)
export const nobody = policy.none();
// (SELECT auth.uid()) = user_id — the column must be uuid
export const owner = policy.isOwner('user_id');
// ((SELECT auth.jwt()) -> 'app_metadata' ->> 'role') = 'admin' — GLOBAL app role, see below
export const platformAdmin = policy.hasRole('admin');
// org_id IN (membership via a SECURITY DEFINER helper on org_members)
export const member = policy.belongsTo('org_id', {
  table: 'org_members', foreignKey: 'org_id', localKey: 'user_id',
});
// same, restricted to members whose role column is admin or manager
export const orgAdmin = policy.belongsTo('org_id', {
  table: 'org_members', foreignKey: 'org_id', localKey: 'user_id', where: { role: ['admin', 'manager'] },
});
// author_id = (SELECT auth.uid()) — either side may be a column or an auth call
export const sameUser = policy.matchesField('author_id', 'auth.uid()');
// raw SQL predicate — always write (SELECT auth.uid()), never bare auth.uid()
export const published = policy.custom("status = 'published'");
// OR / AND
export const ownerOrPublished = policy.any([policy.isOwner('user_id'), published]);
export const ownerAndUnlocked = policy.all([policy.isOwner('user_id'), policy.custom('locked = false')]);
// USING = first rule; WITH CHECK = first AND second rule (the written row must pass both)
export const editOwn = policy.withCheck(policy.isOwner('author_id'), policy.custom('edited = true'));
// { mode: 'replace' }: WITH CHECK = second rule only (the row may leave the first rule)
export const publishDraft = policy.withCheck(
  policy.all([policy.isOwner('author_id'), policy.custom("status = 'draft'")]),
  policy.all([policy.isOwner('author_id'), policy.custom("status IN ('draft', 'published')")]),
  { mode: 'replace' },
);
```

`belongsTo(column)` without `through` checks `profiles.<column>` of the current user (needs a
`profiles` table with that column). Avoid it: it is only safe when users can NEVER write that
column — no `insert` policy on profiles (create profiles from an auth trigger or the service
role) and `trigger.lockColumns({ columns: ['org_id'] })` on profiles. Otherwise a user sets
their own `profiles.org_id` to another tenant's id and joins it; `validate` rejects that with
`BELONGS_TO_PROFILE_WRITABLE`. Use a membership table (`through`) instead.
With `through`, the membership lookup is a generated
`SECURITY DEFINER` function with `SET search_path = pg_catalog, public` (no RLS recursion,
safe on the membership table itself).

Global vs tenant roles — pick the right one:
- Role INSIDE an org/team/workspace ("org admins can delete"): store it in the membership
  table and use `{ scope: 'tenant', roles: ['admin'] }` in `definePermissions`, or
  `policy.belongsTo(col, { ..., where: { role: ['admin'] } })`.
- Platform-wide role ("our staff can read the audit log"): `policy.hasRole('admin')` or a
  role array `['admin']` in `definePermissions`. Both read the JWT `app_metadata.role`
  claim, which only the server can set: `supabase.auth.admin.updateUserById(id,
  { app_metadata: { role: 'admin' } })` (service role) or a custom access token hook.
  The top-level JWT `role` claim is never used (it is the Postgres role `authenticated`).
`validate` warns with `GLOBAL_ROLE_IN_TENANT_TABLE` when a table mixes both.

## definePermissions (centralized RBAC, multi-tenant)

Actions map `read→select`, `create→insert`, `update→update`, `delete→delete`. Levels:
`'public'`, `'*'` (any signed-in user), `'none'`, `'own'` (needs `ownerColumn`), a role array
(GLOBAL app roles from `app_metadata.role`, see above), `{ scope: 'tenant' }` (member of the
row's tenant, needs `tenant` and `tenantColumn`), `{ scope: 'tenant', roles: [...] }` (member
with one of those roles, needs `tenant.roleColumn`), `{ any: [...] }` (OR). Unknown roles throw
at definition time.

Writes are pinned by default (secure unless you opt out):
- `create` also requires `ownerColumn = (SELECT auth.uid())` — nobody can create rows
  attributed to someone else. Opt out with `pinOwnerOnCreate: false` when others assign the
  owner column (e.g. a task's `assignee_id`); pin the real creator column yourself then.
- `update`, and `create` when its level is not already tenant-scoped, also require that the
  user is a member of the row's (new) tenant — an owner cannot move a row into another
  org. Not applied to `create` when `tenantColumn` is `'id'` (the row is the tenant itself).
  Opt out with `pinTenant: false` for resources written by non-members (customers booking
  into a shop).

```ts
import { definePermissions } from 'accessnexus';

export const permissions = definePermissions({
  roles: ['owner', 'editor', 'viewer'],
  tenant: { table: 'team_members', userColumn: 'user_id', tenantColumn: 'team_id', roleColumn: 'role' },
  resources: {
    documents: {
      ownerColumn: 'created_by',
      tenantColumn: 'team_id',
      read: { scope: 'tenant' },
      create: { scope: 'tenant', roles: ['owner', 'editor'] }, // + created_by = auth.uid()
      update: { any: ['own', { scope: 'tenant', roles: ['owner'] }] }, // + stays in a team you belong to
      delete: { scope: 'tenant', roles: ['owner'] },
    },
  },
});

// On the table: policies: permissions.policiesFor('documents')
// One rule:     permissions.can('documents', 'update')
export const documentPolicies = permissions.policiesFor('documents');
export const canUpdate = permissions.can('documents', 'update');
```

## trigger.* builders

```ts
import { trigger } from 'accessnexus';

// BEFORE UPDATE: sets updated_at = NOW()
export const touch = trigger.updatedAt('updated_at');
// BEFORE DELETE: sets deleted_at = NOW() and cancels the delete
// (table option softDelete: 'deleted_at' adds this automatically)
export const softDelete = trigger.softDelete('deleted_at');
// AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE: inserts into audit_log (see the audit-log recipe)
export const audit = trigger.auditLog({ table: 'audit_log' });
// BEFORE UPDATE: API users cannot change these columns (RLS is row-level, not column-level)
export const freezeOwner = trigger.lockColumns({ columns: ['owner_id', 'org_id'] });
// Lock every column except status/position, unless the SQL condition holds (NEW/OLD available)
export const statusOnly = trigger.lockColumns({
  name: 'assignee_scope', // needed when a table has two lockColumns triggers
  except: ['status', 'position'],
  unless: "EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM org_members m WHERE m.org_id = OLD.org_id AND m.user_id = (SELECT auth.uid()) AND m.role = 'admin')",
});
// Custom PL/pgSQL; events: before_/after_ + insert/update/delete; forEach: 'row' | 'statement'
export const lowerEmail = trigger.custom({
  name: 'lowercase_email',
  events: ['before_insert', 'before_update'],
  when: 'NEW.email IS NOT NULL',
  functionBody: 'NEW.email = lower(NEW.email); RETURN NEW;',
});
// security: 'definer' runs as the owner and bypasses RLS — only for trusted side effects
export const addCreator = trigger.custom({
  name: 'add_creator_as_owner',
  events: ['after_insert'],
  security: 'definer',
  functionBody: "INSERT INTO public.team_members (team_id, user_id, role) VALUES (NEW.id, NEW.created_by, 'owner'); RETURN NEW;",
});
```

`trigger.auditLog` and `trigger.softDelete` functions are `SECURITY DEFINER` with
`SET search_path = pg_catalog, public` and schema-qualified targets: the audit table keeps
`insert: policy.none()` (users cannot forge entries). A soft delete is authorized by the
DELETE policy: the generated guard rejects any plain UPDATE by an API user that sets or
clears the soft-delete column (so the UPDATE policy cannot be used to soft-delete or restore);
restore rows with the service role or a `security: 'definer'` RPC. `trigger.lockColumns`
raises SQLSTATE 42501 when a locked column changes; it never blocks the service role,
SECURITY DEFINER code or columns kept by `trigger.updatedAt`. `updatedAt`, `lockColumns` and
`trigger.custom` run as the writing user (INVOKER, RLS applies to what they read/write)
unless `security: 'definer'`. In a definer body schema-qualify tables (`public.team_members`).

Soft-deleted rows stay visible through RLS (only the SDK filters them). To hide them from raw
API reads too, add the condition to `select`, e.g.
`policy.all([policy.isOwner('author_id'), policy.custom('deleted_at IS NULL')])`.

## rpc (Postgres functions)

Pass RPCs as the second argument of `defineSchema`. With a `body`, AccessNexus emits
`CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` (defaults: `plpgsql`, `SECURITY INVOKER`, volatile, pinned
`search_path`, returns `void` when `returns` is omitted) and a typed `client.rpc.<name>()`.
`rpc({ args, returns })` without body only types the client; `rpc()` is a marker for
Database mode. `security: 'definer'` bypasses RLS — check `(SELECT auth.uid())` yourself
(and reject anonymous callers). For definer RPCs AccessNexus revokes EXECUTE from `PUBLIC` and
`anon` and grants it to `authenticated` and `service_role`; pass `allowAnon: true` to keep
anon. Invoker RPCs keep Supabase's default (callable by `anon` and `authenticated`; RLS
applies inside). `validate` warns `UNWRAPPED_AUTH_CALL` for a bare `auth.uid()` in a body.
An argument is a type or `{ type, default }` with a raw SQL default
(`args: { p_limit: { type: 'int', default: '20' } }` → `p_limit INTEGER DEFAULT 20`; callers may
omit it, the client type marks it optional). After one argument with a default, every following
one needs a default too (`INVALID_DEFAULT`).

```ts
import { defineSchema, policy, rpc, table } from 'accessnexus';

export default defineSchema({
  todos: table({
    columns: { id: 'uuid', user_id: 'uuid', done: 'boolean' },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { user_id: 'auth.users.id' },
    policies: {
      select: policy.isOwner('user_id'),
      insert: policy.isOwner('user_id'),
      update: policy.isOwner('user_id'),
      delete: policy.isOwner('user_id'),
    },
  }),
}, {
  rpcs: {
    count_open_todos: rpc({
      returns: 'int',
      language: 'sql',
      body: 'SELECT count(*)::int FROM todos WHERE user_id = (SELECT auth.uid()) AND NOT done;',
    }),
    complete_all: rpc({
      args: { p_user: 'uuid' },
      body: 'UPDATE todos SET done = true WHERE user_id = p_user AND p_user = (SELECT auth.uid());',
    }),
    reset_my_todos: rpc({
      security: 'definer', // bypasses RLS: check the caller first
      body: `IF (SELECT auth.uid()) IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'sign in first' USING ERRCODE = '42501'; END IF;
             DELETE FROM public.todos WHERE user_id = (SELECT auth.uid());`,
    }),
  },
});
```

## defineSeed

```ts
// accessnexus.seed.ts — applied by `accessnexus seed` or `accessnexus push --seed` (never implicitly)
import { defineSeed } from 'accessnexus';
import schema from './accessnexus.schema.js';

export default defineSeed(schema, {
  profiles: [
    { id: '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001', name: 'Admin' },
  ],
});
```

Database mode: `defineSeed<Database>({ table: [rows] })`. Rows whose columns reference
`auth.users.id` provision those users in `auth.users` (email confirmed) with a random,
unknowable password — set `ACCESSNEXUS_SEED_PASSWORD` to log in as them locally. Seeding a hosted
Supabase database (`*.supabase.co` / `*.supabase.com`) is refused without
`--allow-remote-seed`. Seeds upsert by primary key, so re-running is safe.

## defineConfig

```ts
// accessnexus.config.ts — every field optional
import { defineConfig } from 'accessnexus';

export default defineConfig({
  schema: './accessnexus.schema.ts',
  seed: './accessnexus.seed.ts',
  output: {
    dir: './generated',                 // base for the folders below
    migrations: './supabase/migrations',
    sdk: './src/lib/accessnexus',           // where the app imports the client from
  },
  naming: { policyPrefix: 'app' },      // policy names: <prefix>_<table>_<operation>
  generate: { sqlOnly: false, sdkOnly: false },
  adapterOptions: {
    dbUrlEnv: 'SUPABASE_DB_URL',        // env var push/seed read the DB URL from
    deterministic: true,                // omit the "Generated at" header line
    uuidGeneration: 'v7',               // time-ordered uuid PKs via public.accessnexus_uuidv7()
  },
  targets: {                            // push/seed --target <name>
    staging: { adapter: 'supabase', adapterOptions: { dbUrlEnv: 'STAGING_DB_URL' } },
  },
});
```

`uuidGeneration: 'v7'`: migrations define `public.accessnexus_uuidv7()` (RFC 9562 UUIDv7: 48-bit
millisecond timestamp, version 7, random tail) before the first table that uses it. EXECUTE is
revoked from `PUBLIC` and `anon` (so PostgREST does not expose it to anonymous callers) and
granted to `authenticated` and `service_role`; `anon` gets it only when a v7 table's insert
policy lets anonymous users write. There is no `uuid_generate_v7()`.

## SupabaseAdapter (programmatic generation)

Pure functions returning `{ path, content }`; the CLI uses them. Useful in tests.

```ts
import { SupabaseAdapter } from 'accessnexus';
import schema from './accessnexus.schema.js';

const adapter = new SupabaseAdapter({ policyPrefix: 'accessnexus', deterministic: true });
const policies = adapter.generatePolicies(schema);   // <table>_rls.sql
const triggers = adapter.generateTriggers(schema);   // <table>_triggers.sql
const migration = adapter.generateMigrations(schema); // 001_initial.sql (full DDL)
const rpcs = adapter.generateRpcs(schema);           // rpcs.sql
const sdk = adapter.generateClient(schema);          // types.ts + client.ts

export const files = [...policies, ...triggers, ...migration, ...rpcs, ...sdk].map((f) => f.path);
```

## Generated SDK

`createAccessNexusClient(supabase)` wraps a supabase-js client with typed per-table accessors:
`findMany(filter?, { include? })`, `findById(id, { include? })`, `create(row)`,
`update(id, patch)`, `delete(id)` (a real DELETE; on soft-delete tables the trigger sets the
column instead, so the DELETE policy decides), plus
`rpc.<name>(args)` and `auth`. Results are `{ data, error }` like supabase-js. `include`
embeds tables declared in `references`. RLS still applies: the SDK runs as the signed-in user.
`<Table>Create` types make nullable columns, columns with a `default` and an auto-generated
(uuid/bigint) primary key optional; everything else is required.

```ts
import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
import { createAccessNexusClient } from './generated/sdk/client.js';

const db = createAccessNexusClient(createClient('https://xyz.supabase.co', 'public-anon-key'));

export async function example(userId: string) {
  const { data: me } = await db.profiles.findById(userId);
  const { data: projects } = await db.projects.findMany({ org_id: 'some-org-id' }, { include: { org: true } });
  await db.profiles.update(userId, { name: 'New name' });
  const { data: stats } = await db.rpc.get_org_dashboard({ p_org_id: 'some-org-id' });
  return { me, projects, stats };
}
```

## CLI reference

`npx accessnexus <command> [flags]`; `npx accessnexus <command> --help` lists flags.

Flags on every command: `--json` (one JSON object on stdout, nothing else; colors off —
also for `help --json` and `<command> --help --json`),
`--verbose` (debug + stack traces; same as `DEBUG=accessnexus`), `--config <path>`.
Unknown flags and commands are errors (with a did-you-mean hint), never ignored.
Colors are disabled when stdout is not a TTY or `NO_COLOR` is set.

- `init` — scaffold AccessNexus in any Node project (Next.js app/pages, Vite with any framework,
  CRA, or a plain Node/other project): schema (template or imported from the DB),
  `accessnexus.config.ts`, SDK wrappers reusing an existing Supabase client, a `accessnexus` npm
  script, and a AccessNexus block in `AGENTS.md` (plus a pointer in `CLAUDE.md` if present). Without a TTY it requires `--yes`. Flags: `--yes`/`-y`,
  `--src <dir>`, `--sdk <dir>` (default `<src>/lib/accessnexus`), `--prefix <name>`,
  `--db-url <url>`, `--no-introspect`, `--install` (install missing @supabase packages),
  `--force` (overwrite an existing schema), `--no-agents`. Re-running is safe: an existing
  schema is kept (unless `--force`) and the AGENTS.md block is replaced in place. With `--yes`
  in a folder without `package.json` it creates a minimal one. `--db-url` imports each policy
  without ever granting more than the database did: policies for non-API roles
  (`TO service_role`) are skipped, `TO authenticated` adds the signed-in check, RESTRICTIVE
  policies are AND-ed in, anon-only policies become a TODO (denied), and an operation with no
  applicable policy becomes `policy.none()`; a table whose RLS is off in the database gets an
  explicit `enableRLS: false` (with a comment) so `push` does not change it silently — remove
  it to lock the table. Over REST (no `--db-url`) RLS cannot be read: the imported tables
  have no policies, so `push` turns RLS on for all of them, and a table whose RLS was off becomes
  deny-all until you add policies (or `enableRLS: false`). Review the imported rules (comments name the
  source policy) and replace `policy.custom` with semantic builders where possible. The
  original database policies are still there after `init`: Postgres ORs permissive policies,
  so they would keep granting access. `push` therefore refuses with `FOREIGN_POLICIES` while a
  managed table has a policy not named `<prefix>_<table>_<op>`; once the imported rules are
  reviewed, ask the user, then `push --replace-foreign-policies` drops them in the push
  transaction.
  `--db-url` also imports exact column types (`numeric(10,2)`, enums as `enum(...)`, `text[]`
  / `int[]` / `uuid[]`), column defaults, composite primary keys (`compositePrimaryKey`),
  multi-column UNIQUE (as unique `indexes`), FKs to other schemas (`'auth.users.id'`) with their
  `ON DELETE`, RPC parameter defaults, and user triggers as `trigger.custom` (timing, events,
  `FOR EACH`, `WHEN`, `SECURITY DEFINER` kept; `UPDATE OF cols` becomes a WHEN on those columns
  changing). What cannot be expressed is left as a `// WARNING:` comment in the schema, never
  dropped silently: triggers with arguments, disabled, INSTEAD OF / TRUNCATE-only or non-plpgsql
  ones; array/other types with no AccessNexus equivalent (imported as `text`); generated columns;
  multi-column FKs. Imported triggers are recreated as `<prefix>_<table>_<name>`: after `push`
  to the same database the original trigger would still exist and both would fire, so `push`
  refuses with `FOREIGN_TRIGGERS` until the user approves `--replace-foreign-triggers`. Enum columns get AccessNexus's own enum type (`<table>_<column>_enum`).
- `validate` — load + check the schema, write nothing. Flags: `--schema <path>`.
- `generate` — write migrations, policies, triggers, RPCs and the SDK. Files that only differ
  in the `-- Generated at:` line are left untouched. Flags: `--schema`, `--output <dir>` (every
  output folder goes under `<dir>`, overriding the paths in `accessnexus.config.ts` — handy to
  preview into a scratch folder), `--sql-only`, `--sdk-only`, `--prefix <name>`.
- `diff` — what `generate` would change; writes nothing. Same flags + `--check` (exit 1 when
  anything is out of date). It compares the schema with the generated FILES, not the
  database; when a database URL is configured its result carries a `hint` pointing to
  `--against-db`.
- `diff --against-db` — live change plan: connects (same `--url`/`--db-url`/env/`--target`
  resolution as `push`), takes the push advisory lock without waiting (`PUSH_LOCKED` if a
  push is running), BEGINs, snapshots the catalog of everything the schema manages, applies
  exactly what `generate` + `push` would apply (the SQL the current schema generates, through
  the push code path), snapshots again and ROLLs BACK. Nothing persists — no objects, no
  `accessnexus_migrations` rows. Foreign policies/triggers are dropped in the plan only with
  `--replace-foreign-policies` / `--replace-foreign-triggers` (as in push); without them they
  are reported in `blockers`. `--allow-destructive` likewise. `--check` exits 1
  (`LIVE_DB_CHANGES`) when the database would change; a push Postgres would reject exits 1
  (`PUSH_WOULD_FAIL`) with `failed: { file, message, sqlState }`.
- `push` — apply generated SQL in order migrations → policies → triggers → rpcs, tracked in
  `public.accessnexus_migrations`. The whole push (bookkeeping, foreign-policy drops and every
  file) runs in ONE transaction under an advisory lock: if anything fails, nothing from that
  push stays applied. (Exception: a migration that adds an enum value cannot use that value in
  the same push — Postgres forbids it inside a transaction; push the enum change first.) Re-running skips unchanged files and
  re-applies changed policy/trigger/RPC files; editing an applied migration is refused. Before
  touching the database it checks that the generated SQL matches the schema
  (`GENERATED_OUT_OF_DATE`) and that no pending migration destroys data
  (`DESTRUCTIVE_MIGRATION`), and that the role bypasses RLS when the SQL has SECURITY DEFINER
  helpers (`PUSH_ROLE_NO_BYPASSRLS`). It reads `pg_policies` for every table the schema
  manages and refuses (`FOREIGN_POLICIES`, nothing applied) while any policy there is not one
  AccessNexus generates (`<prefix>_<table>_<op>`); `--replace-foreign-policies` drops them in the
  same transaction. Same for triggers not named `<prefix>_<table>_...` (`FOREIGN_TRIGGERS`,
  `--replace-foreign-triggers`). Prints a notice instead of waiting silently when another
  push holds the lock. Flags: `--url <db-url>` (alias `--db-url`), `--dry-run` (lists files and
  destructive statements; when a database URL is set it also rehearses the push of the files
  on disk like `diff --against-db` and returns that plan as `livePlan` — nothing persists),
  `--allow-destructive`, `--replace-foreign-policies`, `--replace-foreign-triggers`, `--seed` (also run the seed), `--allow-remote-seed`, `--output`,
  `--schema`, `--prefix`, `--adapter`, `--target`.
- `seed` — upsert seed rows. Flags: `--seed <path>`, `--url` (alias `--db-url`), `--dry-run` (prints the SQL),
  `--allow-remote-seed`, `--schema`, `--prefix`, `--adapter`, `--target`.
- `help [command]`, `version` (also `--version`). With `--json` both print one object.

Database connections (`push`, `seed`, `diff --against-db`, `init --db-url`) give up after 10 s with
`DB_CONNECTION_FAILED` instead of hanging; set `ACCESSNEXUS_DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=<seconds>` to change it.

Exit codes: `0` success; `1` user-fixable (bad flag, missing file, schema error, missing DB
URL, unreachable DB, SQL rejected, stale output, destructive migration without
`--allow-destructive`, failed seed); `2` internal error
(a AccessNexus bug — rerun with `--verbose` and report the stack).

### --json output shapes

Every result has `ok`, `command` and `version`. Failures add `error` (and keep any partial
result fields, e.g. `issues`, `applied`).

```ts
export interface SchemaIssue {
  severity: 'error' | 'warning';
  code: string;   // e.g. 'UNKNOWN_COLUMN'
  path: string;   // e.g. 'posts.policies.update'
  message: string;
  hint?: string;  // how to fix it
}

export interface ErrorResult {
  ok: false;
  command: string;
  version: string;
  error: { code: string; message: string; hint?: string; stack?: string /* --verbose */ };
  issues?: SchemaIssue[]; // SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED
}

export interface ValidateResult {
  ok: true; command: 'validate'; version: string;
  schemaPath: string;
  mode: 'manual' | 'database';
  tables: Array<{ name: string; columns: number; primaryKey: string | null; rls: boolean; policies: string[]; triggers: Array<{ kind: string; name: string | null }> }>;
  rpcs: string[];
  issues: SchemaIssue[]; // warnings only (errors make ok=false)
  summary: { errors: number; warnings: number };
}

export interface DestructiveStatement {
  file: string;   // migration file
  line: number;
  kind: 'drop_table' | 'drop_column' | 'alter_column_type' | 'drop_type' | 'truncate';
  sql: string;
}

export interface GenerateResult {
  ok: true; command: 'generate'; version: string;
  schemaPath: string;
  mode: 'manual' | 'database';
  files: Array<{ path: string; category: 'migrations' | 'policies' | 'triggers' | 'rpcs' | 'sdk'; status: 'created' | 'updated' | 'unchanged' }>;
  destructive: DestructiveStatement[]; // in migrations written by this run
  summary: { created: number; updated: number; unchanged: number; files: number; tables: number };
  warnings: SchemaIssue[];
}

export interface DiffResult {
  ok: boolean; // false only with --check and pending changes (error.code GENERATED_OUT_OF_DATE)
  command: 'diff'; version: string;
  schemaPath: string;
  changed: boolean;
  destructive: DestructiveStatement[]; // in migrations generate would write
  summary: { added: number; modified: number; removed: number };
  changes: Array<{ path: string; status: 'added' | 'modified' | 'removed'; diff: string }>;
  warnings: SchemaIssue[];
  hint?: string; // set when a database URL is configured: use `diff --against-db` for the live plan
}

export type PlanKind = 'table' | 'column' | 'constraint' | 'index' | 'rls' | 'policy' | 'trigger' | 'function' | 'grant';

export interface PlanChange {
  kind: PlanKind;
  // 'public.notes' (table, rls) | 'public.notes.body' (column) | 'public.notes.<policy|trigger|constraint>'
  // | 'public.<index>' | 'public.fn(uuid, text)' (function) | 'table public.notes' / 'function public.fn()' (grant)
  object: string;
  change: 'added' | 'removed' | 'modified';
  before?: Record<string, unknown>; // normalized catalog properties (absent when added)
  after?: Record<string, unknown>;  // (absent when removed)
  fields?: string[];                // modified: the properties that differ
  // properties per kind:
  //   column:     { type, notNull, default, identity, generated }   (type via format_type, default via pg_get_expr)
  //   constraint: { type, definition }    index: { table, definition }    rls: { enabled, forced }
  //   policy:     { command, permissive, roles: string[], using, withCheck }
  //   trigger:    { timing, events: string[], level, when, function, enabled }
  //   function:   { returns, language, volatility, securityDefiner, strict, config: string[], bodyHash, definition }
  //               ('definition' = pg_get_functiondef, shown but not compared; a body change shows as 'bodyHash')
  //   grant:      { privileges: string[] }  e.g. 'anon=EXECUTE', 'PUBLIC=EXECUTE', 'authenticated=SELECT*' (* = WITH GRANT OPTION)
}

export interface RiskyChange {
  code: 'table_dropped' | 'column_dropped' | 'column_type_changed' | 'column_default_removed'
    | 'column_nullability_relaxed' | 'rls_disabled' | 'policy_dropped' | 'policy_roles_widened'
    | 'policy_permissive_changed' | 'trigger_dropped' | 'function_dropped'
    | 'function_volatility_changed' | 'function_config_changed' | 'function_security_changed'
    | 'grant_widened';
  kind: PlanKind; object: string;
  message: string; // e.g. 'function public.f() STABLE → VOLATILE'
}

export interface LivePlan {
  database: string;              // redacted URL
  wouldApply: string[];          // files push would execute (others are skipped as already applied)
  skipped: Array<{ path: string; reason: 'already_applied' | 'checksum_normalized' }>;
  droppedPolicies: ForeignPolicy[];   // only with --replace-foreign-policies
  droppedTriggers: ForeignTrigger[];  // only with --replace-foreign-triggers
  foreignPolicies: ForeignPolicy[];
  foreignTriggers: ForeignTrigger[];
  blockers: Array<{ code: string; message: string; hint?: string }>; // refusals the real push would stop at
  // (FOREIGN_POLICIES, FOREIGN_TRIGGERS, DESTRUCTIVE_MIGRATION, PUSH_ROLE_NO_BYPASSRLS): the push would apply nothing
  failed: null | { file: string | null; code: string; message: string; sqlState: string | null }; // push would fail
  changed: boolean;
  summary: { added: number; modified: number; removed: number };
  changes: PlanChange[];
  riskyChanges: RiskyChange[];
  persisted: false;              // always: the rehearsal is rolled back
}

export interface DiffAgainstDbResult extends LivePlan {
  ok: boolean; // false with --check and changes (LIVE_DB_CHANGES) or when the push would fail (PUSH_WOULD_FAIL)
  command: 'diff'; version: string;
  schemaPath: string;
  againstDb: true;
  adapter: string; target: string | null;
  generatedUpToDate: boolean; // false: plan is from the schema; run generate before push
  warnings: SchemaIssue[];
}

export interface PushResult {
  ok: true; command: 'push'; version: string;
  dryRun: boolean;
  adapter: string;
  target: string | null;
  plan: Array<{ category: string; files: string[] }>;
  destructive?: DestructiveStatement[]; // --dry-run: in all migration files
  foreignPolicies?: ForeignPolicy[] | null; // --dry-run: null when no database URL (not checked)
  foreignTriggers?: ForeignTrigger[] | null; // --dry-run: { schema, table, trigger }
  wouldRefuse?: boolean;                    // --dry-run: foreign policies/triggers without their --replace-* flag, or livePlan blockers/failed
  livePlan?: LivePlan | null;               // --dry-run: rehearsal of the files on disk; null without a database URL (or unreachable)
  applied: string[];
  droppedPolicies: ForeignPolicy[];         // --replace-foreign-policies
  droppedTriggers: ForeignTrigger[];        // --replace-foreign-triggers
  skipped: Array<{ path: string; reason: 'already_applied' | 'checksum_normalized' }>;
  seed: null | { path: string; status: 'applied' | 'skipped'; authUsers: number; durationMs?: number }; // only with --seed
  // on failure: error.code DESTRUCTIVE_MIGRATION adds destructive[]; GENERATED_OUT_OF_DATE adds
  // stale: Array<{ path: string; status: string }>; FOREIGN_POLICIES adds foreignPolicies[]; FOREIGN_TRIGGERS adds foreignTriggers[];
  // PUSH_FAILED / MIGRATION_DRIFT: applied is [] (rolled back), rolledBack: string[] lists the files
  // that had run, PUSH_FAILED adds failed: string; a failed --seed keeps applied[] and seed.status 'failed'
}

export interface ForeignPolicy {
  schema: string; table: string; policy: string;
  command: string;      // SELECT | INSERT | UPDATE | DELETE | ALL
  permissive: boolean;  // false = RESTRICTIVE
}

export interface SeedResult {
  ok: true; command: 'seed'; version: string;
  dryRun: boolean; seedPath: string; checksum: string; rows: number;
  authUsers: number; // auth.users rows the seed provisions
  applied: boolean;
  sql?: string; // --dry-run
}

export interface InitResult {
  ok: true; command: 'init'; version: string;
  status: 'initialized' | 'already_initialized';
  framework?: string;
  schemaSource?: 'template' | 'database' | 'rest';
  sdkPath?: string;
  policyPrefix?: string;
  installed?: string[]; // packages installed by --install
  files: Array<{ path: string; action: 'created' | 'updated' | 'skipped' }>;
  agents: null | { agentsMd: 'created' | 'updated' | 'unchanged'; claudeMd: 'updated' | 'unchanged' | 'absent' };
  nextSteps?: string[];
}

export interface HelpResult { // help --json, <command> --help --json
  ok: true; command: 'help'; version: string;
  topic: string | null; // the command asked about, null for the overview
  commands: Array<{
    name: string; summary: string; examples: string[];
    flags: Array<{ name: string; kind: 'boolean' | 'string'; value?: string; description: string }>;
  }>;
  exitCodes: Record<'0' | '1' | '2', string>;
  docs: string; // path of this file
}

export interface VersionResult { ok: true; command: 'version'; version: string }
```

## Recipes

### Owner-only table (each user sees and edits only their rows)

```ts
import { defineSchema, policy, table, trigger } from 'accessnexus';

export default defineSchema({
  notes: table({
    columns: {
      id: 'uuid',
      user_id: 'uuid',
      body: 'text',
      created_at: { type: 'timestamptz', default: 'now()' },
      updated_at: 'timestamptz?',
    },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { user_id: 'auth.users.id' },
    indexes: [{ columns: ['user_id'] }],
    triggers: [trigger.updatedAt('updated_at')],
    policies: {
      select: policy.isOwner('user_id'),
      insert: policy.isOwner('user_id'),
      update: policy.isOwner('user_id'),
      delete: policy.isOwner('user_id'),
    },
  }),
});
```

### Public read, authenticated write

Anonymous visitors read published rows: the `select` rule has a branch that needs no user
(`custom('published = true')`), so its policy is granted `TO public`. Writes stay signed-in
only. Do not "fix" a read problem with `select: policy.public()` — that also exposes drafts.

```ts
import { defineSchema, policy, table } from 'accessnexus';

export default defineSchema({
  articles: table({
    columns: { id: 'uuid', author_id: 'uuid', title: 'text', published: 'boolean' },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { author_id: 'auth.users.id' },
    policies: {
      select: policy.any([policy.custom('published = true'), policy.isOwner('author_id')]),
      insert: policy.isOwner('author_id'), // signed in AND writing as themselves
      update: policy.isOwner('author_id'),
      delete: policy.isOwner('author_id'),
    },
  }),
});
```

### Multi-tenant with roles (teams)

Roles live in the membership table (`team_members.role`). The team creator becomes its first
owner through a `security: 'definer'` AFTER INSERT trigger on `teams` — not through an INSERT
rule on `team_members`, which a creator removed by the other owners could replay to rejoin.
Owners add anyone, editors may only add plain members (so nobody can promote themselves).
`definePermissions` pins writes: `projects.created_by` must be the creator and a project can
never move to a team the user is not in; `lockColumns` keeps who/where a row belongs fixed.

```ts
import { definePermissions, defineSchema, policy, table, trigger } from 'accessnexus';

const permissions = definePermissions({
  roles: ['owner', 'editor', 'member'],
  tenant: { table: 'team_members', userColumn: 'user_id', tenantColumn: 'team_id', roleColumn: 'role' },
  resources: {
    teams: {
      ownerColumn: 'created_by',
      tenantColumn: 'id',                          // the row IS the tenant
      read: { any: ['own', { scope: 'tenant' }] },  // creator sees it before joining
      create: '*',                                  // + created_by = auth.uid()
      update: { scope: 'tenant', roles: ['owner'] },
      delete: { scope: 'tenant', roles: ['owner'] },
    },
    projects: {
      ownerColumn: 'created_by',
      tenantColumn: 'team_id',
      read: { scope: 'tenant' },
      create: { scope: 'tenant', roles: ['owner', 'editor'] },
      update: { any: ['own', { scope: 'tenant', roles: ['owner'] }] },
      delete: { scope: 'tenant', roles: ['owner'] },
    },
  },
});

/** Current user is a member of the row's team (optionally with one of `roles`). */
function teamMember(roles?: string[]) {
  return policy.belongsTo('team_id', {
    table: 'team_members', foreignKey: 'team_id', localKey: 'user_id',
    ...(roles ? { where: { role: roles } } : {}),
  });
}

export default defineSchema({
  teams: table({
    columns: { id: 'uuid', name: 'text', created_by: 'uuid' },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { created_by: 'auth.users.id' },
    triggers: [
      // The creator becomes the first owner (runs as the table owner, bypassing RLS)
      trigger.custom({
        name: 'add_creator_as_owner',
        events: ['after_insert'],
        security: 'definer',
        functionBody: "INSERT INTO public.team_members (team_id, user_id, role) VALUES (NEW.id, NEW.created_by, 'owner'); RETURN NEW;",
      }),
      trigger.lockColumns({ columns: ['created_by'] }),
    ],
    policies: permissions.policiesFor('teams'),
  }),
  team_members: table({
    columns: { id: 'uuid', team_id: 'uuid', user_id: 'uuid', role: "enum('owner','editor','member')" },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { team_id: 'teams.id', user_id: 'auth.users.id' },
    onDelete: { team_id: 'cascade' },                     // deleting a team removes its memberships
    indexes: [{ columns: ['team_id', 'user_id'], unique: true }],
    triggers: [trigger.lockColumns({ columns: ['team_id', 'user_id'] })], // owners change roles only
    policies: {
      // Own rows too: INSERT ... RETURNING (what the SDK's create does) must see the new row
      select: policy.any([teamMember(), policy.isOwner('user_id')]),
      insert: policy.any([
        teamMember(['owner']),                                                     // owners add anyone
        policy.all([teamMember(['editor']), policy.custom("role = 'member'")]),    // editors add members only
      ]),
      update: teamMember(['owner']),
      delete: policy.any([teamMember(['owner']), policy.isOwner('user_id')]),     // owners remove, anyone leaves
    },
  }),
  projects: table({
    columns: { id: 'uuid', team_id: 'uuid', created_by: 'uuid', name: 'text' },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { team_id: 'teams.id', created_by: 'auth.users.id' },
    onDelete: { team_id: 'cascade' },
    triggers: [trigger.lockColumns({ columns: ['created_by', 'team_id'] })],
    policies: permissions.policiesFor('projects'),
  }),
});
```

App flow: `db.teams.create({ name, created_by: user.id })` — the creator is now an owner.
Then owners add people with `db.team_members.create({ team_id, user_id, role })`.
This direct add is fine here because co-members see nothing personal about each other. If
co-members can read each other's profiles (email, name), switch to invitations — see
"Visibility derived from sharing a tenant" in the RLS rules below.

Trade-off: `teams.read` includes `'own'` so the creator can read the row the SDK's `create`
returns (`INSERT ... RETURNING` is checked before the AFTER INSERT membership exists). A
creator later removed from the team therefore still sees that one `teams` row (its name),
never its projects or members. If the team name itself is sensitive, drop `'own'` from
`read` and create teams with `db.teams.create(...)` ignoring the returned row (or through a
`security: 'definer'` RPC that inserts and returns the id).

### Child of a tenant resource (tasks under projects)

RLS checks each row against its OWN tenant column, and foreign keys are checked without
RLS. So `tasks` needs its own `org_id` (denormalized, so `belongsTo` can check it), and
something must keep `tasks.org_id` equal to the project's `org_id` — otherwise a member of
org A can create a task in A that points at org B's project (probing B's ids, attaching
rows that cascade with B's data). `validate` warns `TENANT_PARENT_UNCHECKED` when the guard
is missing. Guard it with a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger and freeze both columns:

```ts
import { defineSchema, policy, table, trigger } from 'accessnexus';

const member = policy.belongsTo('org_id', { table: 'org_members', foreignKey: 'org_id', localKey: 'user_id' });
const memberPolicies = { select: member, insert: member, update: member, delete: member };

export default defineSchema({
  orgs: table({
    columns: { id: 'uuid', name: 'text' },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    policies: { select: policy.belongsTo('id', { table: 'org_members', foreignKey: 'org_id', localKey: 'user_id' }) },
  }),
  org_members: table({
    columns: { id: 'uuid', org_id: 'uuid', user_id: 'uuid', role: "enum('admin','member')" },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { org_id: 'orgs.id', user_id: 'auth.users.id' },
    indexes: [{ columns: ['org_id', 'user_id'], unique: true }],
    policies: { select: policy.isOwner('user_id') }, // writes: service role / definer RPCs only
  }),
  projects: table({
    columns: { id: 'uuid', org_id: 'uuid', name: 'text' },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { org_id: 'orgs.id' },
    triggers: [trigger.lockColumns({ columns: ['org_id'] })],
    policies: memberPolicies,
  }),
  tasks: table({
    columns: { id: 'uuid', org_id: 'uuid', project_id: 'uuid', title: 'text' },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { org_id: 'orgs.id', project_id: 'projects.id' },
    onDelete: { project_id: 'cascade' },
    triggers: [
      // Runs as the writing user (INVOKER): a project of another org is invisible
      // through RLS, so it is reported exactly like a project that does not exist.
      trigger.custom({
        name: 'same_org_project',
        events: ['before_insert', 'before_update'],
        functionBody: `
          IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.projects p WHERE p.id = NEW.project_id AND p.org_id = NEW.org_id) THEN
            RAISE EXCEPTION 'project % not found in org %', NEW.project_id, NEW.org_id USING ERRCODE = '23503';
          END IF;
          RETURN NEW;`,
      }),
      trigger.lockColumns({ name: 'lock_tenant', columns: ['org_id', 'project_id'] }),
    ],
    policies: memberPolicies,
  }),
});
```

The same applies to any deeper level (comments under tasks: check `tasks.org_id`).

### Let a user change only some columns

RLS decides WHICH rows a user may update, never WHICH columns: `update: 'own'` on an
assignee also lets them rewrite the title, the assignee or the tenant. Lock the rest with
`trigger.lockColumns` (BEFORE UPDATE, compares OLD and NEW):

```ts
import { defineSchema, policy, table, trigger } from 'accessnexus';

export default defineSchema({
  tickets: table({
    columns: {
      id: 'uuid',
      org_id: 'uuid',
      reporter_id: 'uuid',
      assignee_id: 'uuid?',
      title: 'text',
      status: { type: "enum('open','doing','done')", default: "'open'" },
    },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { reporter_id: 'auth.users.id', assignee_id: 'auth.users.id' },
    triggers: [
      // Nobody re-attributes a ticket or moves it to another org
      trigger.lockColumns({ name: 'lock_identity', columns: ['reporter_id', 'org_id'] }),
      // The assignee may only change status; the reporter may change anything else
      trigger.lockColumns({
        name: 'assignee_scope',
        except: ['status'],
        unless: 'OLD.reporter_id = (SELECT auth.uid())',
      }),
    ],
    policies: {
      select: policy.any([policy.isOwner('reporter_id'), policy.isOwner('assignee_id')]),
      insert: policy.isOwner('reporter_id'),
      update: policy.any([policy.isOwner('reporter_id'), policy.isOwner('assignee_id')]),
      delete: policy.isOwner('reporter_id'),
    },
  }),
});
```

For a multi-step change that must stay consistent, prefer a `security: 'definer'` RPC that
checks the caller and updates only what it should.

### Audit log

`trigger.auditLog({ table })` inserts `(table_name, operation, old_data, new_data,
changed_at)` into the audit table from a `SECURITY DEFINER` function, so the audit table needs
exactly those columns (others nullable or defaulted) and should block API inserts with
`policy.none()`. `validate` reports `AUDIT_TABLE_MISMATCH` (wrong columns, an error) and
`AUDIT_INSERT_OPEN` (users could forge entries, a warning).

```ts
import { defineSchema, policy, table, trigger } from 'accessnexus';

export default defineSchema({
  invoices: table({
    columns: { id: 'uuid', owner_id: 'uuid', amount: 'decimal' },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    references: { owner_id: 'auth.users.id' },
    triggers: [trigger.auditLog({ table: 'audit_log' })],
    policies: {
      select: policy.isOwner('owner_id'),
      insert: policy.isOwner('owner_id'),
      update: policy.isOwner('owner_id'),
      delete: policy.none(),
    },
  }),
  audit_log: table({
    columns: {
      id: 'bigint',
      table_name: 'text',
      operation: 'text',
      old_data: 'jsonb?',
      new_data: 'jsonb?',
      changed_at: { type: 'timestamptz', default: 'now()' },
    },
    primaryKey: 'id',
    policies: {
      select: policy.hasRole('admin'),   // platform staff (app_metadata.role)
      insert: policy.none(),             // only the trigger writes (SECURITY DEFINER)
      update: policy.none(),             // append-only
      delete: policy.none(),
    },
  }),
});
```

## RLS rules agents must not break

- Every table reachable from the client has `policies`; use `policy.none()` for operations
  that must be blocked. Never "fix" a permission error by removing policies, adding
  `enableRLS: false` or using `policy.public()` for writes.
- A tenant-scoped row that references another tenant-scoped row (tasks → projects) needs a
  same-tenant guard trigger (see "Child of a tenant resource"; `TENANT_PARENT_UNCHECKED`).
- Never put private columns (email, phone) in a table whose `select` is
  `isAuthenticated()`/`public()`: on Supabase anyone can sign up and read them.
- Never use `policy.public()` (or `'public'`) for insert/update/delete unless the user asked
  for anonymous writes (`validate` warns `PUBLIC_WRITE`).
- A table keyed by the user id (`profiles.id` → `auth.users.id`) inserts with
  `policy.isOwner('id')`, never `isAuthenticated()` — that lets anyone create another
  user's row (`USER_ROW_INSERT_OPEN`).
- Never write a bare `auth.uid()` / `auth.jwt()` in `policy.custom` or RPC bodies — always
  `(SELECT auth.uid())` (evaluated once per query instead of once per row).
- `policy.isOwner` columns are `uuid`; reference `auth.users.id` or `profiles.id`.
- Use `withCheck(using, check)` to add conditions on the written row; it keeps `using` in
  `WITH CHECK`. Only use `{ mode: 'replace' }` when the row may legitimately leave `using`.
- Keep the write pins of `definePermissions` (`pinOwnerOnCreate`, `pinTenant`); disable one
  only for a concrete reason and pin the right column yourself.
- Never let a member grant a role equal to or above their own: restrict inserts/updates of
  the membership table with `policy.custom("role IN (...)")` (see the multi-tenant recipe).
- Visibility derived from sharing a tenant ("org mates can see my profile") is only private
  if joining a tenant needs the person's consent. If admins may insert any `user_id` into
  the membership table, anyone can create a tenant, add a stranger and read their data as a
  "co-member". In that case add people only through an accepted invitation (a
  `security: 'definer'` RPC that checks the invited, confirmed email) and set the membership
  table's `insert` to `policy.none()`; otherwise keep personal columns out of co-member reads.
- Never add a "bootstrap" INSERT rule on the membership table ("the creator may add
  themselves as owner"): it stays valid forever, so a removed creator can rejoin. Add the
  first member with a `security: 'definer'` AFTER INSERT trigger on the tenant table.
- RLS cannot restrict columns. Freeze owner/creator/tenant columns and limit what partial
  editors may change with `trigger.lockColumns`; an UPDATE rule never does it.
- Org/team roles are tenant roles (`{ scope: 'tenant', roles }`), not `hasRole`.
- The `select` rule must admit rows the user just inserted/updated: the SDK's `create` and
  `update` return the row (`INSERT/UPDATE ... RETURNING`), which fails with an RLS error
  otherwise. On a membership table, add `policy.isOwner('user_id')` to `select`.
- Never use `belongsTo(col)` without `through` while users can write `profiles.<col>`
  (`BELONGS_TO_PROFILE_WRITABLE`).
- Membership checks go through `belongsTo` with `through` / `definePermissions` tenants —
  they compile to `SECURITY DEFINER` helpers with a pinned `search_path` that avoid RLS
  recursion. Do not re-implement them with `policy.custom` subqueries on the same table.
  (Trigger conditions such as `lockColumns({ unless })` are the exception: they are raw SQL
  run as the caller, outside any policy, so an `EXISTS` on the membership table is the way
  to write them — the membership table's own `select` policy still applies.)
- `security: 'definer'` RPCs/triggers and the service role bypass RLS: check the caller inside.
- Do not edit generated SQL to change behavior; change the schema and regenerate. Applied
  migrations are immutable — `push` refuses drift.

## Troubleshooting by error code

- `SCHEMA_NOT_FOUND` — no schema at the path: create `accessnexus.schema.ts`
  (`npx accessnexus init --yes`), pass `--schema`, or set `schema` in `accessnexus.config.ts`.
- `SCHEMA_NO_DEFAULT_EXPORT` — end the file with `export default defineSchema({...})`.
- `SCHEMA_INVALID` — a builder rejected the definition (bad identifier, unknown reference,
  unknown role in definePermissions); the message names the table/field.
- `SCHEMA_VALIDATION_FAILED` — see `issues[]`; fix each `path` as its `hint` says. Common
  codes: `UNKNOWN_COLUMN`, `UNKNOWN_TABLE`, `UNKNOWN_COLUMN_TYPE`, `OWNER_COLUMN_NOT_UUID`,
  `INVALID_POLICY_RULE` (wrote `'public'` instead of `policy.public()`),
  `UNKNOWN_POLICY_OPERATION` (`read`/`create` used as policy keys), `EMPTY_COMBINATOR`,
  `MISSING_COLUMNS`, `AUDIT_TABLE_MISMATCH`, `RPC_IN_TABLES`, `INVALID_TRIGGER`,
  `INVALID_REFERENCE`, `INVALID_IDENTIFIER`, `RESERVED_IDENTIFIER` (rename `order` → `orders`),
  `INVALID_PRIMARY_KEY` (`compositePrimaryKey` with fewer than two columns, together with
  `primaryKey`, or with `softDelete`),
  `UNKNOWN_TABLE_KEY` (typo such as `polices:`, or tables nested under a `tables:` key —
  pass them directly to `defineSchema`), `INVALID_ENUM_VALUE` (a `belongsTo` `where` value
  that is not in the membership column's enum, e.g. a misspelled role).
  `INVALID_DEFAULT` (`default` is raw SQL: write `"'todo'"`, not `'todo'`),
  `INVALID_ON_DELETE` (unknown action, no foreign key, or `'set null'` on a NOT NULL column),
  `CASCADE_INTO_SOFT_DELETE` (use `'restrict'`), `DUPLICATE_TRIGGER` (give a second
  `lockColumns`/`custom` trigger its own `name`), `BELONGS_TO_PROFILE_WRITABLE` (use
  `through`, or make `profiles.<col>` server-written only), `RLS_DISABLED_WITH_POLICIES`
  (remove `enableRLS: false`).
  Warnings: `NO_POLICIES` (table is deny-all for the API — add policies if the client uses
  it), `RLS_DISABLED` (`enableRLS: false`: the table is open to the anon key),
  `TENANT_PARENT_UNCHECKED` (add the same-tenant guard trigger), `NO_PRIMARY_KEY`, `UNWRAPPED_AUTH_CALL` (bare `auth.uid()` in a
  custom policy or an RPC body), `PUBLIC_WRITE` (insert/update/delete open to anonymous
  visitors through `policy.public()`), `USER_ROW_INSERT_OPEN` (use `policy.isOwner('id')`),
  `AUDIT_INSERT_OPEN`, `GLOBAL_ROLE_IN_TENANT_TABLE`, `SCHEMA_EMPTY`.
- `SCHEMA_LOAD_FAILED` / `CONFIG_LOAD_FAILED` / `SEED_LOAD_FAILED` — the file threw while
  running or imports a package that is not installed; fix the named file/import.
- `MODULE_SYNTAX_ERROR` — TypeScript/syntax error at the location shown. `TS_LOADER_MISSING`
  — esbuild (a accessnexus dependency) is missing: reinstall with `npm install -D accessnexus`.
- `CONFIG_NOT_FOUND` / `CONFIG_INVALID` — fix `--config` or the config's default export.
- `UNKNOWN_COMMAND`, `UNKNOWN_FLAG`, `MISSING_FLAG_VALUE`, `INVALID_FLAG_VALUE`,
  `UNEXPECTED_ARGUMENT`, `INVALID_FLAGS` — follow the hint / `--help`.
- `GENERATED_OUT_OF_DATE` — `diff --check` or `push` found generated files that do not match
  the schema: run `generate` (review `diff`), then retry.
- `DESTRUCTIVE_MIGRATION` — a pending migration drops a table/column or changes a column
  type. Nothing was applied. If it is a rename, rename in the schema; otherwise confirm with
  the user (and a backup) before `push --allow-destructive`.
- `NOTHING_TO_PUSH` — run `generate` first (or fix `--output`).
- `DB_URL_MISSING` — pass `--url` or set `SUPABASE_DB_URL` (or `ACCESSNEXUS_DB_URL`/`DATABASE_URL`).
- `PG_DRIVER_MISSING` — `push`, `seed` and `init --db-url` need it: `npm install -D pg`.
- `PUSH_ROLE_NO_BYPASSRLS` — the connected role does not bypass RLS, which the generated
  SECURITY DEFINER helpers need. Nothing was applied. Connect as `postgres` (Supabase
  Session pooler string) or `ALTER ROLE <role> BYPASSRLS` as a superuser.
- `SEED_REMOTE_BLOCKED` — seeding a hosted Supabase project; use a local database or pass
  `--allow-remote-seed` if the project is disposable.
- `DB_CONNECTION_FAILED` — wrong URL/password/network; for Supabase use the Session pooler
  string; local databases may need `?sslmode=disable`. A host that never answers fails after
  10 s (`ACCESSNEXUS_DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT=<seconds>`).
- `FOREIGN_POLICIES` — a table the schema manages has RLS policies AccessNexus did not
  generate (listed in the message and `foreignPolicies`). Nothing was applied. Permissive
  policies OR together, so they would keep granting access. Port any rule still needed into
  the schema, ask the user, then `push --replace-foreign-policies` (drops them in the push
  transaction).
- `FOREIGN_TRIGGERS` — a table the schema manages has triggers AccessNexus did not generate
  (`foreignTriggers`). Nothing was applied. They would fire next to the generated ones (after
  `init --db-url`, the imported copy and the original both run). Port what is still needed
  (`trigger.custom`), ask the user, then `push --replace-foreign-triggers`.
- `PUSH_FAILED` — Postgres rejected a file (message has the SQL error; `failed` names it). The
  whole push was rolled back: nothing from it is applied (`applied` is `[]`, `rolledBack` lists
  the files that had run). Fix the schema, `generate`, `push` again.
- `PUSH_WOULD_FAIL` — `diff --against-db` rehearsed the push and Postgres rejected a file
  (`failed.file`, `failed.message`, `failed.sqlState`). Nothing was persisted. Fix the schema
  (or the database state) and plan again.
- `LIVE_DB_CHANGES` — `diff --against-db --check` found that push would change the database;
  the plan (`changes`, `riskyChanges`) is in the result.
- `PUSH_LOCKED` — the live plan does not wait for a running push; retry when it finishes.
- `MIGRATION_DRIFT` — an applied migration file was edited: restore it, change the schema,
  `generate` a new `__changes` migration.
- `SEED_NOT_FOUND` / `SEED_EMPTY` / `SEED_FAILED` — create/fix `accessnexus.seed.ts`; seed after
  push. With `push --seed`, the SQL was already pushed when the seed fails.
- `ADAPTER_NOT_FOUND` / `ADAPTER_AMBIGUOUS` / `ADAPTER_UNSUPPORTED` / `TARGET_NOT_FOUND` —
  only the `supabase` adapter exists. `TARGET_INVALID` — the named entry in
  `config.targets` has no `adapter`; add `adapter: 'supabase'` to it.
- `INIT_NOT_INTERACTIVE` — add `--yes`. `INIT_NEEDS_INPUT` — pass the flag named in the hint.
  `INIT_DETECT_FAILED` — run init in the project root (the folder with package.json), or
  create one (`npm init -y`, or `init --yes` creates a minimal one).
- `INTERNAL_ERROR` (exit 2) — a AccessNexus bug: rerun with `--verbose`, report the stack.

## Limits (v0.1.0)

- Only the Supabase adapter exists. Database mode does not generate DDL migrations.
- Migrations are generated from snapshot diffs; renames are detected heuristically — read
  `diff` output before pushing destructive changes (`-- Destructive:` comments).
- The live plan (`diff --against-db`) covers the managed tables and the functions the
  generated SQL defines or the managed triggers call; it does not snapshot other objects
  (enum types, extensions, unrelated schemas). It reflects what push does: an applied
  migration or an unchanged policy/trigger/RPC file is skipped, so drift made directly in
  the database after a push is not undone by push and does not show in the plan.
- The rehearsal really executes the SQL inside a transaction: it takes the same locks as a
  push (brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks on altered tables) until the ROLLBACK.
- Identifiers are emitted unquoted: lowercase snake_case (one optional leading `_`), no reserved
  keywords.
- RLS is row-level: it cannot restrict which columns an UPDATE changes — use
  `trigger.lockColumns` (see the recipe).
- Foreign keys are `ON DELETE NO ACTION` unless `onDelete` says otherwise.
- Each `enum(...)` column gets its own Postgres type (`<table>_<column>_enum`); cast between
  them in SQL (`v.role::text::org_members_role_enum`).
- GRANT/REVOKE: `security: 'definer'` RPCs are not executable by `anon` unless `allowAnon`.
  Membership helpers are revoked from `PUBLIC`/`anon` and granted to `authenticated`; a
  helper used by a policy that also admits `anon` (`TO public`) is granted to `anon` too,
  which is safe because it returns false when `auth.uid()` is null. Invoker RPCs and tables
  keep Supabase's default grants.
- More prose and examples: `node_modules/accessnexus/README.md`.
